### Description

Sooner or later every R user hits the same wall: you need to do the same thing many times — an analysis for each species, a plot for each group, the same cleaning for every file. The usual answer is copy-paste, which is slow and easy to get wrong.

In this hands-on workshop you'll learn the two skills that fix this:

- **Writing your own functions** — wrapping repeated code into a function with arguments, defaults, and a return value
- **Iterating with `purrr`** — using `map()` and friends to run a function over many inputs at once, instead of copy-pasting or looping

We work through practical examples together, and you'll refactor repetitive code into a function you can apply across many inputs.

## Resources

### Workshop materials

The workshop repo has all demo scripts, exercises, and solutions:

[github.com/selinaZitrone/functions-iteration-workshop](https://github.com/selinaZitrone/functions-iteration-workshop)

### Writing functions

- [R for Data Science on Functions](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/functions): a practical introduction to functions
- [Advanced R, Functions](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/functions.html): a deeper dive once you're comfortable

### Iteration with purrr

- [purrr website](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/): full reference and articles
- [purrr cheatsheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/purrr.pdf): the whole family on one page
- [R for Data Science on Iteration](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/iteration): `map()` and other iteration iteration tools

**More purrr tools:**

- [`map2()` / `pmap()`](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/reference/map2.html): iterate over two or more inputs at once
- [`safely()` / `possibly()`](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/reference/safely.html): keep going when one element throws an error
- [Parallel processing in purrr 1.1.0](https://tidyverse.org/blog/2025/07/purrr-1-1-0-parallel/) and [`furrr`](https://furrr.futureverse.org/): run a map across multiple CPU cores
